sections.description: A complete, white-label loyalty and referral program for WooCommerce. Customers earn points on every purchase, redeem them for dollar-value discounts at checkout, and invite friends via unique referral codes. Includes a floating rewards widget, in-cart / checkout banners, a My Account rewards tab, 5 transactional emails, HPOS-compatible order handling, admin analytics with Chart.js, CSV import/export, direct WPLoyalty migration, and a credit-on-signup queue for pending customer balances. Fully theme-agnostic — every store-visible element is override-safe against aggressive theme CSS.
sections.changelog:
1.5.1

Changed

  • Stores update with nothing to configure. Releases are now published to the public jesssqui/wc-loyalty-engine-releases repo, and stores read its info.json (from raw.githubusercontent.com, so GitHub's 60-an-hour anonymous API limit doesn't apply) and download the zip from its public release. The WCLE_GITHUB_TOKEN constant and wcle_github_token filter from 1.5.0 are gone: no store needs a token or a wp-config.php edit. The source repository stays private
  • WordPress auto-updates are switched on for the plugin once per store, the first time an admin opens wp-admin, so releases install on their own. A store admin who switches them off keeps that choice
  • Update checks every 6 hours instead of 12
  • The release workflow builds the zip and info.json (bin/build-metadata.php) into the release on this repo, needing no secret. bin/publish-latest.sh then copies the release to the public repo: zip first, info.json second (and never backwards), so no store is told about a zip that isn't there yet. It runs from a Mac with one gh command and no clone, or automatically in the workflow once a RELEASES_REPO_TOKEN secret exists

Added

  • wcle_update_metadata_url filter: where a store checks for updates; return '' to switch update checks off on a site

1.5.0

Added

  • Updates from GitHub. Each install now checks this repository's releases and offers new versions as a normal WordPress update ("Update now" on the Plugins screen, the Updates page, and WordPress auto-updates if they're switched on for this plugin). The repository is private, so a site needs define( 'WCLE_GITHUB_TOKEN', '…' ); in wp-config.php with a read-only token; without it nothing changes except a notice on the Plugins screen. Built on the bundled Plugin Update Checker 5.7 (MIT) in lib/plugin-update-checker/. Only the release zip is ever installed, never GitHub's source archive
  • Release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml). Pushing to main with a version that has no release yet checks every PHP file parses, builds wc-loyalty-engine-<version>.zip with bin/build-zip.sh, and publishes release v<version> with this file's matching section as the notes. Pushes that don't change the version do nothing. The header Version: and WCLE_VERSION must match or the run fails
  • wcle_github_token filter, for sites that keep the token somewhere other than wp-config.php

Security

  • Referral codes are random. Codes were built from the member's first name (ADAM-REF, ADAM-REF2 …), so a first-time buyer with no referrer could type a common name at checkout and get the friend discount. New codes are 8 random characters from an alphabet without look-alikes (0/O, 1/I/L): about 850 billion combinations against the existing limit of ~10 attempts per IP every 5 minutes
  • Existing name-based codes are replaced once, on the first wp-admin page load by a store manager after updating. Each old code is kept in the wcle_legacy_referral_codes option (user ID → old code) for tracing or restoring, and the wcle_random_codes_migrated flag is only set when every code was replaced, so a partial run retries. Referral links (?ref=…) use a separate random token and keep working; only the typed code changes. Codes brought in by the WPLoyalty import are not name-based and are left alone

1.4.0

Added

  • Public API for other plugins in includes/wcle-api.php, so a point of sale (GWND Register) can share this plugin's balances without touching its classes: wcle_api_version(), wcle_get_program() (earn rate, campaigns, excluded categories, points per dollar, redemption minimum and maximum), wcle_get_customer() (balance and earn/redeem bans), wcle_get_balance_cents(), wcle_record_transaction() and wcle_get_transaction(). Amounts are integer cents of reward value
  • wcle_record_transaction() is idempotent by reference: every call carries a unique reference, and recording the same reference again returns the first transaction and writes nothing, so a retried sync can never double-credit. It can reverse an earlier transaction by its reference, refuses to overdraw unless told otherwise, applies points expiry to earns, and fires the usual actions so emails and webhooks behave as they do for website orders
  • wcle_handles_order filter: return false and the plugin leaves that order's points alone (no automatic earn on completion, no refund clawback, no status reversal), for orders whose points another plugin records itself. Bonuses and referrals are unaffected
  • reference column on wcle_transactions (unique, NULL for the plugin's own rows), added on upgrade
